title: Black Wall Street, Ep. 2 — One Shot
evidence_boundary: Survivor testimony of the documented 1921 Tulsa Race Massacre. The narrator and her family are fictional; every surrounding event follows the documented record. Spiritual framing is her perception and never blames victims.
desired_movement: From unaware comfort to witnessing how a lie, a newspaper, and a mob unmade a city - while the spirit of Greenwood stays unbroken.
grounding: Greenwood Avenue, the Drexel Building elevator, the Tulsa Tribune, the courthouse line, the Frisco tracks.
invitation: Follow all ten parts - one survivor telling the whole story, start to finish.
era_style: 1921 documentary, black and white with hand-tinted moments

scenes.text: Now. Where did I leave you, child? Tuesday evening, May thirty-first, 1921. A boy in a cell, a lie in the newspaper, a mob collecting like storm water. And Greenwood sitting down to supper, not knowing.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, evening street, long shadows, 1920s

scenes.text: That headline ran at three o'clock. By dark it wasn't news anymore, it was scripture — every man repeating it added a verse. A rumor is a prayer to the wrong god, baby. And white Tulsa prayed it all night.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, 1921 newspaper folded on a wooden table beside wire reading glasses and an oil lamp, heavy dark headline block, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: By seven-thirty they were at the courthouse. By nine, near two thousand. Understand what a mob is, sugar: men who traded their minds for a mood. One fear, wearing a thousand hats.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, dense crowd of men, hats, pushing forward

scenes.text: Sheriff McCullough did his job that night. I will say it plain. Killed the elevator, barricaded the stairs, set riflemen up top, and told that crowd nobody was taking his prisoner. A rare man, holding a rare line.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, jail stairwell, deputy silhouette holding a rifle behind an iron gate, hard side light, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: Word crossed the Frisco tracks, and Greenwood held council — at the Stradford, at the Tulsa Star where Mr. Smitherman ran his press. Veterans. France had taught them their lives were worth defending.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, Greenwood men gathering outside a storefront office

scenes.text: Twenty-five of them rode to the courthouse about nine, rifles honest on their shoulders, and offered the sheriff help protecting Dick. He turned them away polite, and they went home orderly. First trip. There were two.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, seven Black World War One veterans in uniform standing beside a touring car at night, rifles shouldered, resolute, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: Then a telephone rang with a lie in it — the mob is storming the jail, somebody said. It wasn't so. Not yet. But fear don't check its sources, child. Fear just packs.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, candlestick telephone, switchboard operator

scenes.text: Seventy-five made the second trip, near ten o'clock. Against two thousand. Arithmetic did not matter anymore to men done kneeling. They offered once more. Once more, turned away. And on the turning away — it happened.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, open touring cars filled with men at night, glowing headlamps, slight motion blur, 1921, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: An old white man grabbed at a tall veteran's pistol. What you doing with that gun, boy. Wrong man. Wrong night. Wrong word. They wrestled over it, and it went off.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, courthouse crowd, jostling, faces close

scenes.text: One shot, child. To this day nobody can name whose finger. My daddy said later it didn't matter. Two thousand men had already fired it in their minds. That bullet was just catching up.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, two men's hands gripping one army revolver, tight closeup, harsh contrast light, 1921, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: The street came apart in seconds. Men died in the first minute of it, both colors. Ours fell back toward Greenwood fighting a rearguard the whole way, outnumbered twenty to one.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, night street chaos, muzzle flashes, men running

scenes.text: And white Tulsa went shopping. Broke into pawnshops and hardware stores and armed itself on credit it never meant to settle. They robbed their own stores to come kill us — and wrote us down as the criminals.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, shattered pawnshop window at night, empty wooden gun racks inside, broken glass on the sidewalk, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: The police station pinned badges on the mob. Special deputies, they called them. Told them to get a gun and get busy. The law didn't break that night, sugar. It enlisted.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, police station steps, men milling

scenes.text: By midnight the Frisco tracks were a battle line. Ours on the north side, theirs on the south. The same steel that had always told Tulsa who was who, now deciding who would live till morning.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, railroad tracks at night receding into darkness, signal lamp glow, rails shining, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: In our house, nobody slept. Men came carried and bleeding to Daddy's door, because the hospital was not for us. Mama's apron went dark by midnight. I was eight, rolling bandages, learning what a bullet asks of a body.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, lamp-lit home interior, figures moving fast

scenes.text: Daddy never raised his voice once, the whole night. Fear is a poor surgeon, Opal — that's all he said to me. Keep your hands slow. I have kept my hands slow through every terrible thing since. It works, child.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, open leather physician bag with steel instruments laid on white cloth, oil lamp light, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: Out in the dark, carloads ran our streets shooting into porches and windows. The first fires went up along Archer near one o'clock. When our firemen came, guns turned them back. Let it burn was the policy now.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, automobile headlights racing dark residential street

scenes.text: From the upstairs window I watched a light lean on the sky and asked Mama was it morning already. No, baby, she said. That's not morning. First lie my mother ever told me. It surely was a kind of morning.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, distant fire glow above dark rooftops seen past a lace window curtain at night, high contrast, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: Our men took positions where they could — the mill, the hill by the standpipe, the belfry of Mount Zion Baptist. That church was fifty-two days old, sugar. Dedicated in April, with a mortgage the size of heaven.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, silhouettes on rooftops and a grain elevator

scenes.text: Remember that church. You and me are going to cry over her tomorrow. But that night her new brick held our watchmen and her basement held our prayers, and both of them were loaded.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, new brick church with twin towers at night, moonlit, imposing and serene, 1921, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: Toward four o'clock came a quiet like held breath. Thousands of armed men had ringed the tracks, waiting on a signal we did not know was coming. Machine guns set on the hills. Airplanes fueled at the field.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, railyard before dawn, still and gray

scenes.text: Some of our men prayed that hour. Some cleaned rifles. Don't let anybody tell you those are different activities, child. Not that night they weren't.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, silver pocket watch open in a weathered palm, closeup, warm lamplight, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone

scenes.text: Five oh-eight in the morning. June the first. A whistle screamed across the dark, long and mean, and two thousand throats answered it.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, locomotive releasing steam, whistle cord

scenes.text: Whatever that whistle meant to the men who blew it, to us it meant one thing. The end of the world was punctual.
scenes.image_prompt: hand-tinted 1921 photograph, dawn horizon turning deep red over black rooftop silhouettes, delicate watercolor tint over black and white silver print, vintage postcard style, soft muted colors

scenes.text: They came across the tracks at a run, firing as they came. And behind them the sun rose red, child, like it was ashamed to be caught watching.
scenes.query: 1920s archival film, men surging across tracks at a run, period recreation

scenes.text: Daddy looked at Mama over my head and said, real quiet: Willa, put her shoes on. That's enough for tonight, baby. Next time — the morning the sky caught fire. You go on and rest now. I won't.
scenes.image_prompt: hand-tinted 1921 photograph, doorway silhouette of a mother kneeling to lace a small child's shoes, golden dawn light through the door, delicate watercolor tint over black and white silver print, vintage postcard style, soft muted colors

scenes.text: That was part two of Black Wall Street. Ten parts, one story, all here on this channel. If you came in late, go back and start with The Elevator. And meet me at part three, baby — the morning the sky catches fire.
scenes.image_prompt: authentic 1921 documentary photograph, stack of round film reel canisters beside a burning oil lamp on a wooden desk, black and white silver gelatin print, fine film grain, period-correct 1920s clothing and architecture, dignified historical tone
